html:
George Tupou I was the chief Tāufaʻāhau who united Tonga by 1845 and reigned as its first modern king until 1893. He founded the royal house that still rules.

He became a Methodist in 1831, taking the name George, and won the civil wars between rival chiefly lines. As king he freed commoners from forced labour to chiefs in 1862, gave every man a right to land, and in 1875 granted a written constitution.

His treaties with European powers helped keep Tonga from becoming a colony while Fiji and Samoa were taken. His descendant Sālote later made the monarchy famous abroad.
